title: The Red Horse within the Flames
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Heiji, Kazuha, Kogoro Mouri, Ran) omitted by convention, as is Inspector Yuminaga (arson-squad inspector who plays the same case-local investigating-officer role as Inspector Megure elsewhere, and whose questions are answered by the omitted detective cast). Episode 326 has no subtitle file locally (only 0325.txt and 0327.txt exist in subs_resolved/) -- this rebuild is based on those two episodes only; whatever aired in 326 (likely more of the household-visitor investigation) is not reflected here. The old cases/ file's culprit call (Akira Morozumi) is CORRECT and matches the transcript -- no discrepancy there -- but it modeled the case as 4 generic suspects all `knows` a single victim with an `unspecified` motive and one clue; this rebuild adds the real mechanism: the four red horse figurines are four separate physical props (three planted by Akira to build a fake serial-arsonist pattern, one an unrelated accidental survivor from fire #1 that coincidentally kicked off the media legend and led Genda to suspect his own sleepwalking), a delayed-ignition light-bulb/tissue/match rig giving Akira a drinking alibi, two red-herring peddler subplots (Soga's bugged vase, Keiko's bugged crystal ball, sold to Genda at inflated prices -- unrelated to the murder but explaining the listening-device red herring), and the base-plate/figurine-leg forensic match plus the bug-elimination logic that actually identifies Akira. Genda's own backstory (his father died years earlier in an unrelated fire caused by a dropped cigarette, which is why he was seen searching a park bench and why Mouri trusted his innocence) involves only omitted detective-cast characters as the other party, so it is kept as an attribute on Genda's node rather than a separate person/edge. Per the 2026-08 batch-8+ convention, order/temporal_frame/years_before_present are omitted from edges. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Base plate in Ryoko's hand matches the leg shape of the Okuho-chou horse figurine, tying the murder scene directly to the planted third fire.

Fires 2-4 share an identical MO (oil through a window plus a red horse figurine); fire 1's cause and figurine origin don't match that pattern at all -- it was a coincidental survivor, not part of a real series.

Soga's vase-bug and Keiko's crystal-ball-bug were left untouched (their sellers would have reclaimed their own devices before suspicion could fall on them), but a third bug was hidden in Genda's phone line -- proving a separate eavesdropper who needed to monitor Genda and Soga, not sell to Genda.
